Read the records of a bigWig file that overlap intervals

Source: R/intervals-import.R
gintervals.import_bigwig.Rd

Reads the records of a bigWig file over a set of intervals without importing the file into a track. Only the data blocks that the file's index places over the intervals are read and decompressed, so reading a few thousand regions of a large bigWig is fast.

Usage

gintervals.import_bigwig(file, intervals = NULL)

Arguments

file

path to a bigWig file.

intervals

intervals to read the records of. NULL reads all the records of the file.

Value

A data frame with columns chrom, start, end and value.

Details

Each record that overlaps intervals is returned once, whole (not clipped to the intervals), also when it overlaps several of them, and the records are sorted by chrom and start. The full-resolution records are read (bedGraph, variableStep and fixedStep sections alike), never the zoom levels; zero-length records are skipped. As in gtrack.import, chromosome names are matched to the database through its aliases (chr1 <-> 1, ...), a file none of whose chromosomes the database has is an error, and a record that runs past the end of its chromosome is clipped to it (dropped if it starts past it) with a warning. With intervals = NULL, records on chromosomes the database lacks are skipped with a message, or a warning if one of them looks like a primary chromosome. If no record overlaps intervals, the result is a data frame of no rows with the same columns (a sparse signal often has no record over a region); with intervals = NULL, a file of no records is an error.

The result works directly as the source of a value-based virtual track (gvtrack.create), which computes the signal over intervals without importing the file. func = "sum" adds up the values of the records an interval touches, each counted once; "weighted.sum" weighs each by the number of its bases inside the interval, which is the sum of the signal over the interval's bases. An interval that no record overlaps gets NaN from sum, weighted.sum, avg, min, max and lse, and 0 from size and exists.

See also

gtrack.import, gvtrack.create, gintervals.import_bed.

Examples


gdb.init_examples()
# dense_track.bw holds only chr1 and chr2, positions 0-5000, of the example
# database's dense_track: no record overlaps intervals outside them
f <- system.file("extdata", "dense_track.bw", package = "misha")
peaks <- gintervals(c(1, 2), c(1000, 3000), c(1500, 3600))
signal <- gintervals.import_bigwig(f, peaks)
head(signal)
#>   chrom start  end value
#> 1  chr1  1000 1050  0.10
#> 2  chr1  1050 1100  0.00
#> 3  chr1  1100 1150  0.02
#> 4  chr1  1150 1200  0.00
#> 5  chr1  1200 1250  0.00
#> 6  chr1  1250 1300  0.02

# the signal summed over each peak's bases, without importing the file
gvtrack.create("sig", src = signal, func = "weighted.sum")
gextract("sig", peaks, iterator = peaks)
#>   chrom start  end sig intervalID
#> 1  chr1  1000 1500  27          1
#> 2  chr2  3000 3600  74          2
